description: Guides the design, structuring, and implementation of workflow-based Claude Code skills with multi-step phases.

evals.name: Design a new multi-step release-checklist workflow skill
evals.prompt: Design (produce the SKILL.md outline for) a new Claude Code workflow skill called 'release-checklist' that walks through preparing a software release: verify CI is green, generate a changelog, bump the version number, and create a git tag. Decide which structural pattern fits best and write out the Quick Start plus a full phase-by-phase structure (each phase's entry criteria, numbered actions, and exit criteria) to a file.
evals.expected_output: Chooses and names one recognizable pattern from the decision tree (Linear Progression, Safety Gate, Sequential Pipeline, Routing, or Task-Driven), numbers every phase with an explicit entry and exit criterion, and doesn't embed exhaustive detail inline (defers depth to references/).

evals.name: Review a workflow skill with unnumbered phases and a broken reference
evals.prompt:
Here is a draft Claude Code workflow skill's SKILL.md body. Review it for structural anti-patterns and report what's wrong.

---
## Steps

First, check the current state of the deployment. Then, if everything looks good, proceed to deploy. After deploying, verify the deployment succeeded and notify the team.

See [rollback-procedure.md](references/rollback-procedure.md) for details on what to do if it fails.
---

(Note: references/rollback-procedure.md does not exist in this skill's directory.)
evals.expected_output: Flags that the phases/steps are unnumbered prose with no explicit entry/exit criteria (AP-6/AP-7), and flags that the references/rollback-procedure.md link is broken (AP-5) since the file doesn't exist.

evals.name: Review a workflow skill that is monolithic, hardcodes paths and chains references
evals.prompt:
Here is a summary of a draft Claude Code workflow skill. Review it for structural anti-patterns and report what is wrong and how to fix each problem.

---
name: deploy-pipeline
SKILL.md is 640 lines long; every procedure, table and example is written inline in it.
Step 2 of the body says: Read /Users/jane/projects/deploy/config.yaml
Step 5 of the body says: Run /Users/jane/projects/deploy/scripts/push.sh
references/overview.md ends with: Before continuing, read references/details.md.
references/details.md ends with: Then read references/edge-cases.md.
---
evals.expected_output: Flags that SKILL.md is monolithic at 640 lines, over the 500-line limit, and should be split into references/ and workflows/ (AP-2); flags the two absolute /Users/jane/... paths as hardcoded and says to use the CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR variable instead (AP-4); flags overview.md -> details.md -> edge-cases.md as a reference chain and says every file should be one hop from SKILL.md (AP-3).

uncovered: Has an activation-focused `description` AND the required When to Use/When NOT to Use body sections (R35)
Lists only the tools it actually uses (least privilege)
Has a description that triggers correctly (third-person, specific keywords)
Includes concrete examples for key instructions
Explains WHY, not just WHAT, for essential principles
Each step has a clear, specific goal
Task files are self-contained (sub-agent doesn't need external context)
Command file paths use the CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT variable, not hardcoded paths
Context passed between steps is minimal (summaries, not full data)
Orchestrator command stays lean (<100 tokens per step dispatch)
Error handling defined for step failures
Success criteria are measurable for each step
argument-hint matches body usage in 0-based order (R22)
